messages:
incident-bot: Paging: automated alert — EU inference cluster p95 latency spiked above 1.2s for the last 6m, error rate steady but tail latency is high. Severity: potential customer impact. @eng-oncall please ack.

alex: acked. oncall taking. seeing p95 ~1.3s on the eu-west-1 model pool (gptx-medium).

sam: noted. any correlating infra alerts? disk, network, or GPU saturation?

alex: GPUs at ~60% util, no mem OOMs. Scheduling queue backlog up ~25%. NVlink errors none. Kernel crash rate 0.

maria: traffic spike? region routing?

alex: 10:30 UTC we got a traffic burst from a single customer — heavy long-context streaming. Prefix cache miss rate jumped.

jamal: sounds like KV cache churn + long-context requests causing CPU overhead in router, increasing latency. Recommend enabling aggressive prefix cache for that customer and temporarily route their traffic to a dedicated pool.

lina: if route change needed, CS needs a short customer note. prepping a draft.

sam: runbook step 2: check autoscaler decisions and scale-up events. alex, can you force one additional node in the eu dedicated pool and enable burst?

alex: triggering scale-up now: 
```
# forcing scale-up
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/eu-west-1/scale -d '{"delta":1}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

alex: scale request accepted, new node booting (ETA ~90s).

incident-bot: Note: scaling operation may take up to 2m to be reflected in telemetry.

maria: while we wait, can we apply routing rule to divert requests from customer 'heavy-ctx-999' to the low-latency fallback model (gptx-small) for 15 minutes? That reduces per-request cost but will lower latency.

sam: I can add a temporary policy: route by header X-Customer-ID=heavy-ctx-999 -> model=gptx-small, region=eu-west-1. Will update policy in 30s.

alex: applied policy. Observe: incoming rate for that customer dropping on gptx-medium and moving to gptx-small. p95 on gptx-medium improving to 0.95s. overall cluster p95 trending down.

jamal: good. still do we want to add a KV prefix cache TTL bump to reduce misses? quick config: cache.prefix_ttl=600 -> 1800 for that customer.

sam: done. config change pushed to routers.

lina: CS draft for customer note (short):
```
Hi there — we observed elevated latency for some requests from your account starting ~10:30 UTC. We've routed your traffic to a low-latency fallback to restore performance; this may slightly alter response length/format. We're monitoring and expect normal performance within ~20–30 minutes. Reach out if you see anything unexpected. — Redwood Inference Support
```

maria: internal status page draft for posting to customers: (for ops/status)
```
Summary: Elevated tail latency affecting EU inference region due to high long-context request volume from a single customer. Impact: increased response time (p95 up to ~1.3s) for a subset of requests. Mitigation: temporarily routed traffic to fallback model and scaled dedicated pool; applied cache TTL to reduce KV churn. ETA for full recovery: 20–40 minutes. Next update: in 15 minutes or sooner. Workaround: none required; we have proactively routed impacted traffic.
```

alex: telemetry shows p95 for region at 0.87s now, error rate unchanged. Scale completed, new node healthy.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to P2 (degraded performance, mitigations applied).

jamal: recommend extended monitoring for 2 hours and add an automated rule to detect customer long-context rate > X and trigger routing if seen again. Filing a JIRA: INF-4521 for longer-term mitigation and quota changes.

sam: assigning follow-ups: 1) jamal create INF-4521 (done), 2) infra to assess autoscaler tuning (alex), 3) CS to send final customer note if they ask (lina).

lina: CS will hold until we confirm recovery then send the customer the notice above and offer a short call if needed.

alex: closing loop: cluster p95 stable at 0.8s for last 4m, request backlog returned to normal.

maria: please post status page update now with the draft.

sam: posting now to status.redwood.ai (draft copied).

incident-bot: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1958001234

alex: handing off to night oncall @jamal for monitoring. I'm available if anything flares.

jamal: ack. I'll keep a 2h watch and escalate if p95 > 1s for 5 consecutive minutes.

lina: thanks team — CS notified. I'll loop back if the customer replies.

sam: quick internal-template for post-incident notes (ops summary):
```
- Incident id: 1958001234
- Timeline: 10:30 UTC spike -> 10:31 mitigate routing -> 10:33 scale request -> 10:35 cache TTL bump -> 10:45 stable
- Root cause: high long-context request volume causing prefix cache churn and router CPU pressure
- Mitigation: customer traffic routed to fallback model, autoscale +1, cache TTL increase
- Customer impact: transient increased latency for a subset of requests; no errors or data loss
- Action items: INF-4521 (auto-route on threshold), autoscaler tuning, post-mortem within 48h
```

maria: I'll create the incident postmortem doc and assign owners. thanks all. :thumbsup:
